$documentation: Enumerated exceptions for the blocking dependency-audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs,
run by the `audit` job in .github/workflows/test.yml). Policy narrative lives in
docs/supply-chain-policy.md section 7.
Every advisory `bun audit` reports must either be FIXED or appear here. There is no
third option and no global escape hatch: this file replaced a `continue-on-error` +
`|| echo` pair whose justification ('all in harper transitive deps') was true when it
was written, carried no expiry, and was still silently passing the build long after it
had stopped being true.
Adding an entry is a REVIEWED act, not a way to get green. Each one must carry the
advisory id, what pulls it in, why it cannot be fixed from this repo, a hard expiry
date, and the concrete condition that retires it. The gate checks: required fields
present and non-blank (all fields but sources are strings); a GHSA- id of letters,
digits and hyphens in canonical casing (uppercase prefix, lowercase rest); no
duplicate entry for an advisory (same package, sources, introducedBy); a known class
and a non-empty array of known sources; at most one entry per advisory and package
naming bun or npm-install;
no bun source for vendor-pinned; real added and expires dates with expires after
added; added no later than today and no later than the advisory's first snapshot
day (today when no snapshot has it), and a first history day for its id that is a
real calendar date no later than today; a configured severity cap, with an
overCapApproval required when the lifetime exceeds it and validated whenever present
(all four members present as non-blank strings, real dates, approvedOn no later than
today, unexpired, covering
the entry, within the cap); and removeWhen trimmed to at
least 20 characters. Reviewers judge whether the reason is true and the retirement
condition is concrete. An entry whose span exceeds its severity's cap needs a valid
over-cap approval; that approval cannot extend expiry past approvedOn plus the cap, so
nothing is parked further than today plus the cap. The ceilings (critical 30,
high 60, moderate and low 180 days) are pinned in scripts/audit-gate.mjs; the policy
block below may set a shorter lifetime for a severity, never a longer one.
When an entry expires the build FAILS and a human re-decides. That is the mechanism
working. Re-dating an entry without re-reading its reason is how this file rots back
into the thing it replaced.

classes.no-patch-published: No fixed version exists on the registry yet. Verified by the gate on every run: if a patched version ships, this entry fails and must be actioned.
classes.vendor-pinned: A patched version exists upstream, but the vulnerable copy is resolved inside a vendored dependency whose tree we do not control. Retired by moving the vendor, not by bumping the leaf.
classes.remediation-available: A patched version exists AND we could take it. Deliberately deferred to a separate, test-gated dependency PR so a security gate lands independently of a lockfile change. Shortest leash of the three.

entries.reason: Split 2026-11-01 from the vendor-pinned entry for this advisory: bun.lock resolves through this repository's root overrides, so its copy is remediable here. bun.lock resolves @fastify/static 9.3.0, pulled only by harper 5.3.1's ^9.1.3. A patched release exists (10.1.1, or 10.1.2, which also clears GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj; npm's latest is 10.1.8), and a root override could move bun.lock's copy to it, but that forces a major version outside harper's declared range onto the operations server harper itself mounts. Deferred to a separate, test-gated dependency PR. Same use and exposure as the npm-install entry for this advisory. flair does not import @fastify/static.
entries.removeWhen: A dependency PR moves bun.lock's @fastify/static to a patched release with harper's operations server tested, or flair moves to a harper release that declares a patched @fastify/static range, or flair stops depending on harper.

overCapApproval.reason: A root override to 10.x would change only flair’s bun tree, not the copy an npm install gets, and is declined. The npm copy is fixed only by a harper release that updates it.

entries.reason: Split 2026-11-01: this entry now covers only the npm-install observation, and the bun.lock copy has its own remediation-available entry. Renewed 2026-11-01 after re-reading against harper 5.3.1 and harper 5.3.4, the version flair pins (package.json:69) (renewed 2026-09-25, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-22). harper 5.3.1's npm-shrinkwrap pins @fastify/static 9.3.0 (node_modules/harper/node_modules/@fastify/static in an npm install of flair), and npm honours that pin over root overrides; harper 5.3.4 declares the same ^9.1.3 and bundles 9.3.0. The fix is 10.1.1 (10.1.2 for GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj; npm's latest is 10.1.8), and the 9.x line still ends at 9.3.0, so no fixed release is inside ^9.1.3. Where it is used: harper 5.3.1 imports it only in dist/server/operationsServer.js:53 and registers it once (:208), on the operations server, with a fixed root of harper's own Studio assets (studio/web); flair sets localStudio enabled: false (src/commands/init.ts:1039,1194). Authentication on the operations server is per-route preValidation (GET /api/openapi/rest :217, POST / :220), so no guard is tied to the paths the plugin serves. harper's application-port static handler uses send, not this plugin (dist/server/static.js:12), and flair's config.yaml declares no static handler. flair does not import @fastify/static. The default flair install binds the operations server to 127.0.0.1 (DEFAULT_OPS_BIND_HOST, src/cli.ts) plus a domain socket; an operator who widens the bind with --ops-bind or FLAIR_OPS_BIND makes the plugin reachable beyond loopback.
entries.removeWhen: flair moves to a harper release whose installed tree resolves @fastify/static >=10.1.1 (>=10.1.2 also retires GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj), whether pinned by its npm-shrinkwrap or shipped in its bundle; or flair stops depending on harper. harper 5.3.1 and 5.3.4 both declare ^9.1.3, and the 9.x line ends at 9.3.0.

overCapApproval.reason: The latest harper release still bundles the vulnerable copy; the fix is a harper release that updates it.

entries.reason: Renewed 2026-11-01 after re-reading against the ADK consumer install, which resolves @google/adk 2.4.0, npm's latest. Resolved inside @google/adk's own tree, which we do not control: @google/adk 2.4.0 depends on @google-cloud/vertexai ^1.12.0 (1.12.0), which requires google-auth-library ^9.1.0 (9.15.1); that requires gaxios ^6.1.1 and gtoken ^7.0.0, and each gaxios 6.7.1 copy requires uuid ^9.0.1. The install has two uuid 9.0.1 copies. This entry covers node_modules/@google-cloud/vertexai/node_modules/uuid, the copy its introducedBy chain resolves to; node_modules/gtoken/node_modules/uuid, reached through gtoken 7.1.0's own gaxios, has its own entry. The fix, uuid 11.1.1, is outside ^9.0.1, and the gaxios 6.x line ends at 6.7.1. A direct dependency or override in @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair cannot reach these nested copies. flair's adapter does not import uuid.
entries.removeWhen: a @google/adk release's dependency tree resolves every uuid copy >= 11.1.1, or the ADK consumer install no longer reports this advisory
